chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: Repertoire, the blues label, Joe Springer
summary: He played every song but Dixieland, got labeled a blues player from Blue Harlem, and kept Joe Springer a long time.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: What kind of songs did you play with your own band when you started?

Yeah, a lot of blues. I got that's where my name got hung up as a blues player on account of Blue Harlem, 'cause that was the first record I made that did any selling, I mean it was among the first. And it sold very good, and like I said Fred Robins used it for his theme song, just that particular part that I played. So that gave me a little label there. But I mean when I hit a club I played everything that we played along with Art Tatum. Same type of thing. Everything you could name, you know.
Did you have Joe Springer in your band also?
Yeah, he was a good player --- quiet fella. --- He stayed with me a long time.
